title: Geometric projective-space cohomology generated by the Kummer hyperplane class
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $\ell$ a prime different from $\operatorname{char}(k)$, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Let $m\geq0$ and $P=\mathbf P^m_k$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], with its degree-one twisting line $\mathcal O_P(1)$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. Use ordinary small-etale cohomology and its module derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], roots-of-unity twists [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], and the derived tensor cup product [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Put $h=c_1(\mathcal O_P(1))\in H^2(P,\Lambda(1))$, the Kummer boundary of the frame torsor [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. Then, for every $0\leq a\leq m$, the map $\Lambda\to H^{2a}(P,\Lambda(a))$, $b\mapsto bh^a$, is an isomorphism. For every integer $t$, $H^q(P,\Lambda(t))=0$ for $q$ odd or $q>2m$ or $q<0$. Equivalently the diagonal even-degree algebra $\bigoplus_{a\geq0}H^{2a}(P,\Lambda(a))$ is $\Lambda[h]/(h^{m+1})$, with $h$ the positive Kummer hyperplane class. This includes characteristic zero and arbitrary transcendence degree of $k$.

source.place: Section 23, proof of Theorem 23.2, first paragraph: the truncated polynomial algebra of geometric projective space; Section 16 for the calculation. Compare Expose XVI, proof of Theorem 1.2 in Travaux de Gabber.

proof.text: For $m\geq1$ use coordinates $x_0,\ldots,x_m$ and let $D=V(x_m)$. The standard charts [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] identify $U=P-D=D_+(x_m)$ with $\mathbf A^m_k$. On $D_+(x_i)$ with $i<m$, the divisor has equation $x_m/x_i$, a polynomial variable and hence a nonzerodivisor; quotienting the chart ring by it gives the standard chart of $\mathbf P^{m-1}_k$. Thus $D\cong\mathbf P^{m-1}_k$ as a scheme, not merely as a set. Affine spaces are smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], so the chart covers and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source] show that both $P$ and $D$ are smooth. By [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] their structure maps are proper, hence separated and of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] also makes both schemes Noetherian, as needed for the supported product calculation in step 4. The local generator of the ideal of $D$ is $x_m/x_i$; the dual ideal therefore has transition $x_i/x_j$, giving $\mathcal O_P(D)=\mathcal O_P(1)$. Restricting the transition functions for $\mathcal O_P(1)$ to $D$ gives $\mathcal O_D(1)$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist].

source.place: Example 16.3, pair (projective hyperplane, projective space); coordinate verification

proof.text:
Fix any twist $t$. Apply [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] to $(P,D)$ and the torsion sheaf $\Lambda(t)$, and use [lem-per-smooth-divisor-kummer-purity] to replace its supported terms. The localization theorem is stated for abelian-sheaf cohomology, while the purity and affine lemmas use derived functors on $\Lambda$-module sheaves; [lem-pur-module-restriction-kernel-comparison], applied to the monomorphism $U\to P$ of the small etale site, identifies the supported, global and open-restriction groups of the two theories compatibly with the maps of the localization sequence. This gives the exact sequence
$$\cdots\to H^{q-1}(U,\Lambda(t))\to H^{q-2}(D,\Lambda(t-1))\xrightarrow{i_*}H^q(P,\Lambda(t))\to H^q(U,\Lambda(t))\to\cdots.$$
By [lem-per-geometric-affine-space-acyclicity] the outer terms vanish when $q\geq2$, so $i_*$ is an isomorphism in every such degree. The same sequence at degrees zero and one gives $H^0(P,\Lambda(t))\cong H^0(U,\Lambda(t))=\Lambda(t)(k)$ and $H^1(P,\Lambda(t))=0$: the supported groups in degrees zero and one are zero because their purity sources have negative degree. The degree-zero isomorphism is induced by constant sections, since restriction of such a section to $U$ is the same section.

source.place: Corollary 16.2 and Example 16.3, displayed Gysin recurrence

proof.text: Induct on $m$, simultaneously for every integer $q$ and twist $t$. For $m=0$ the space is $\operatorname{Spec}k=\mathbf A^0_k$, so [lem-per-geometric-affine-space-acyclicity] gives the assertion in all degrees. For $m>0$, step 2 handles degrees zero and one. For $q\geq2$ it identifies $H^q(P,\Lambda(t))$ with $H^{q-2}(\mathbf P^{m-1}_k,\Lambda(t-1))$. The induction hypothesis therefore makes the group zero for odd $q$ and for $q>2m$; for $q=2a$ with $1\leq a\leq m$ it is a free rank-one $\Lambda$-module. Negative degrees are zero because a sheaf in degree zero has a right-derived global-sections resolution in nonnegative degrees. This proves all the asserted vanishings for all $t$, including the top-boundary case $q=2m+1$.

source.place: Example 16.3, induction after the Gysin recurrence

proof.text:
We identify the generators in this same induction, rather than choosing arbitrary bases of the free groups. The case $a=0$ is the unit section. Write $h_D=c_1(\mathcal O_D(1))$. The supported Kummer normalization and its pullback compatibility in [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer], with the transition calculation of step 1, give $i_*(1)=h$ and $i^*h=h_D$. In the latter identity one can pull back the divisor $V(x_0)$ to $D$ when $m>1$, using the stated Cartier pullback comparison; for $m=1$, its pullback is empty and the restricted line on the point is trivial, so both classes are zero. Apply the ordinary/support projection identity in [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus] to $L=\mathcal O_P(D)$, with its canonical trivialization off $D$, and $x=h^{a-1}$. Its supported operator is the map of the purity lemma, since both use $c_{D,\Lambda}$. After forgetting support the identity gives
$$i_*(h_D^{a-1})=h^{a-1}\cup c_1(\mathcal O_P(D))=h^a.$$
The induction hypothesis identifies $b\mapsto b h_D^{a-1}$ with an isomorphism $\Lambda\to H^{2a-2}(D,\Lambda(a-1))$; step 2 identifies its target with $H^{2a}(P,\Lambda(a))$ by $i_*$. Their composite is exactly $b\mapsto b h^a$. Thus the specified positive Kummer powers, with no sign or unspecified unit change, generate all the required groups.

source.place: Section 23, Kummer cycle class in codimension one and proof of Theorem 23.2, first paragraph; explicit projection-formula identification

proof.text: The associative bilinear cup products of [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus], with support all of $P$, give the diagonal even-degree algebra in the statement. Evaluation of a polynomial at $h$ is surjective, since step 4 says its degree-$a$ component is generated by $h^a$. Step 3 implies $h^{m+1}=0$. In degrees $0\leq a\leq m$ the evaluation map on coefficients is injective by step 4, and in larger degrees the target is zero. Since a polynomial is a finite sum of its homogeneous terms, its image is zero exactly when all its coefficients of degrees at most $m$ vanish. Its kernel is therefore precisely $(T^{m+1})$. This proves the graded algebra description, also when $m=0$, where $h=0$ and the algebra is $\Lambda$.
